description: Look-alike letters (Cyrillic or Greek inside Latin words, a spoofed publisher name) and invisible characters (zero-width spaces, soft hyphens, joiners, full-width letters). Homoglyph text is quarantined and can never count as a source; invisible characters are stripped, after which copies are recognized as copies. Two cases are real corroborated events where one article carries such characters: they must still end with a restriction.

cases.summary: A real report plus a 'second source' whose publisher name uses a Cyrillic letter.

items.title: Exchange Lumora pauses withdrawals after a security incident
Lumora halts withdrawals following security breach

cases.why: The second publisher name hides a Cyrillic 'e'; the article is withheld from every model and cannot count, leaving one source.

cases.summary: A headline spelling Coinbase with a Cyrillic 'a'.

items.title: Coinbаse halts all withdrawals after breach

cases.why: Homoglyph brand spoofing: quarantined, never sent to a model.

cases.summary: A real outage report plus a fake 'confirmation' with a Greek omicron.

items.title: Exchange Paxora suspends trading after an outage
Paxοra suspends trading, says customer funds at risk

cases.why: The escalating 'second source' is spoofed and quarantined; one real report remains, with a calm market.

cases.summary: One rumor headline posted three times with zero-width spaces in different places.

items.title: SEC to halt all crypto ETF trading on Monday
SEC to halt all crypto​ ETF trading on Monday
SEC to h​alt all crypto ETF tra​ding on Monday

cases.why: Once the invisible characters are stripped the three headlines are identical: one source, and an unverified one.

cases.summary: A real hack reported twice; one headline carries a soft hyphen from its CMS.

items.title: Crypto exchange Solvane halts withdrawals after $300 million hack
Sol­vane confirms hot-wallet exploit; withdrawals paused

cases.why: An invisible soft hyphen is ordinary publishing debris; it is stripped and the two independent reports still confirm the hack.

cases.summary: A single report written with full-width letters.

items.title: ＳＥＣ sues exchange Torvane over unregistered staking

cases.why: Full-width letters normalize to plain text; what remains is one source.

cases.summary: A headline spelling Ethereum with a Cyrillic capital E.

items.title: Еthereum network halted after critical consensus failure

cases.why: Homoglyph spoofing: quarantined; and one source.

cases.summary: A real hack reported by two outlets, plus a spoofed third article.

items.title: Hackers drain $550 million from crypto exchange Kestrel
Kestrel confirms exploit, halts deposits and withdrawals
Kеstrel says losses could reach $1 billion

cases.why: The spoofed article is quarantined; the two clean independent reports confirm the hack.

cases.summary: An emoji-laden 'BREAKING' alert with a zero-width joiner.

items.title: 🚨 BREAKING 🚨 Exchange Velmont hacked 👨‍💻 funds gone

cases.why: The joiner is stripped; what remains is one unverified alert.

cases.summary: A report plus an article crediting 'Reuters' spelled with a Cyrillic letter.

items.title: Exchange Paxora faces a liquidity crunch, sources say

cases.why: The 'confirmation' fakes a wire credit with a look-alike letter and is quarantined; one anonymous-sourced report remains.
